findings.title: Unverified Method — sensorsService.updateLastSeen()
findings.problem: The design claims to call sensorsService.updateLastSeen() method in multiple places. Verification Result: This method does NOT exist in the actual sensors.service.ts file. Grep search returned zero matches.
findings.impact: Implementation will fail with 'method does not exist' error.
findings.fix: Implement updateLastSeen() in SensorsService or remove all calls to it and document that lastSeen tracking is not implemented. Design must specify which option.

findings.title: Missing Dependency — ScheduleModule Not Imported
findings.problem: The design requires @Cron decorator for daily cache cleanup job. Verification Result: ScheduleModule is NOT imported in src/iot/iot.module.ts.
findings.impact: Cron job will not execute. TypeScript compilation may succeed but runtime will fail silently.
findings.fix: Add explicit import instruction: import { ScheduleModule } from '@nestjs/schedule' and add ScheduleModule.forRoot() to IotModule imports array.

findings.title: Ambiguous — AnalyticsService Not Injected in DashboardService
findings.problem: The design adds a cron job in DashboardService that calls this.analyticsService.getPiezoStatistics(). Verification Result: AnalyticsService is NOT injected in DashboardService constructor.
findings.impact: broadcastPiezoStatistics() method will fail with 'this.analyticsService is undefined' error.
findings.fix: Provide explicit constructor injection code and verify that DashboardModule imports AnalyticsModule.

findings.title: Unspecified Behavior — Frontend TanStack Query Retry Logic
findings.problem: The design assumes TanStack Query is configured with retry logic. Verification Result: No QueryClient configuration with retry settings was found in frontend code.
findings.impact: If retry is not configured, API failures will not retry, contradicting the design's error handling strategy.
findings.fix: Provide QueryClient configuration or verify existing setup with retry: 3 and appropriate retryDelay.

findings.title: Missing Specification — ESP32 Global Variables Initialization
findings.problem: The design introduces three new global variables (previousCapVoltage, previousTriggerTime, cumulativeStepCount) but does not specify where to declare them or how to initialize them in setup().
findings.impact: Variables declared inside functions will lose state between calls. Uninitialized variables will cause incorrect power/energy calculations on first reading.
findings.fix: Add explicit declaration in global variables section and initialization code in setup() after initial voltage reading.

findings.title: Ambiguous Signature — getPiezoStatistics() Query Parameters
findings.problem: The parameters are optional but the design doesn't specify: (1) Default behavior when parameters are omitted, (2) Whether sensorId is a string or ObjectId, (3) Whether startDate/endDate are ISO strings or Date objects.
findings.impact: Frontend and backend may have mismatched assumptions about parameter types and defaults.
findings.fix: Provide explicit signature with types: async getPiezoStatistics(sensorId?: string, startDate?: string, endDate?: string): Promise<PiezoStatisticsDto> and document default behavior.

findings.title: Unspecified — Power Validation Skip Logic
findings.location: Section 1.4 (HTTP POST), note about backend validation
findings.problem: The design states backend must skip P=V×I validation for piezo, but doesn't specify HOW to detect piezo readings. The note suggests checking source === 'hardware' OR using dedicated piezo endpoint, but these are two different approaches.
findings.impact: If power validation is enabled globally, piezo readings (with current=0) will fail validation even though the design explicitly sends current=0.
findings.fix: Choose ONE approach and specify exactly where to implement it: either skip validation in dedicated piezo endpoint or modify validateReadingData() to accept isPiezo parameter.

findings.title: Missing Error Handling — ESP32 Buffer Overflow
findings.problem: The design declares a buffer for 10 readings but doesn't specify what happens when buffer is full (11th reading arrives). The comment 'Buffer current reading' has no implementation.
findings.impact: Buffer overflow could cause memory corruption or silent data loss.
findings.fix: Provide complete buffer insertion code with overflow handling: either discard oldest (shift array) or discard new reading. Design must specify which.

findings.title: Ambiguous — Step Milestone Cache Key Format
findings.problem: The cache key uses template literal syntax but sensorId is an ObjectId (MongoDB type). The design doesn't specify whether to convert to string or use .toString().
findings.impact: JavaScript will convert ObjectId to '[object Object]', causing all sensors to share the same cache entry.
findings.fix: Use explicit conversion: const cacheKey = `piezo_steps_${sensorId.toString()}`; or document that sensorId parameter is already a string.

findings.title: Inconsistent Terminology — 'Trigger' vs 'Footstep'
findings.problem: The design uses 'trigger' (technical term) and 'footstep' (user-facing term) interchangeably.
findings.fix: Standardize terminology: Internal/Technical use 'trigger', User-Facing use 'footstep'. Keep piezo:trigger event name but add message: 'Footstep detected' for clarity.

findings.title: Potential Performance Issue — Milestone Check Every Reading
findings.location: Section 2.3, checkStepMilestones() called in receivePiezoReading() flow
findings.problem: Milestone checking happens synchronously for every reading. If sensor sends readings at high frequency (>1 Hz), this could add latency.
findings.fix: Add note acknowledging this was considered: 'Performance: Milestone check is O(1) Map lookup. If >10 readings/sec become common, consider batching or async queue.'

findings.title: Magic Number — Capacitor 90% Threshold
findings.problem: Hardcoded 90% threshold. Could be made configurable like other thresholds.
findings.fix: Add to .env: PIEZO_CAPACITOR_FULL_THRESHOLD=0.9 or document why 90% is a fixed hardware constraint.

findings.title: Incomplete Documentation — WebSocket Event Payload Schema
findings.problem: Design shows example payloads in TypeScript interfaces but doesn't document all fields completely. For example, piezo:trigger event has sensorLocation but doesn't specify if this is string or nested object.
findings.fix: Add complete TypeScript interface definitions with field types and descriptions for all WebSocket event payloads.
